items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I took Johnny Letman on a tour in Europe a few days ago... Two years ago I took Johnny Letman on a tour for Honestier... Now, I took Johnny Letman to Europe, '77, I think it was.

ctx.x: Where was the lineage? Where was the direct line so that you could see, Dan...where...what happened in 1908, '09, '10, '11, '12, '13, '14, '15 should not be a break in the history of blacks in jazz. I say this, and I say it quite candidly, that I've been very, very disturbed that Duke Ellington died several years ago...do they play his music? Yes. And I'm sure they get the royalties. I'm sure that he was astute enough to have that kind of arrangement, and lawyers and...to take care of that. But what about…
I took Johnny Letman on a tour in Europe a few days ago...and incidentally, I want to talk to you about Europe, too,

I want to tell you some of the things...good things that I think have happened. Two years ago I took Johnny Letman on a tour for Honestier, and we had Ronnie Cole on the drums, we had George Kelly, we had Bill Pemberton, and I played the piano,and Fred Alonzo the trombone player, a young man from New Orleans...a good trombone player that's one of the few trombone...promising trombone players that I've heard from Louisiana. I've heard him in Bern, Switzerland, year before last with Wally Davenport. I heard him in…
